why: Wheels can't fix any of the three. At the 4.5 cm maximum radius the wheel climbs only about 3.61*1.5 = 5.4 cm on concrete, under the 5.5 cm step. It spans at most a 9 cm gap with a 4.5 cm dip, so the belly still grounds in the trench, and its patch stays near 20 cm2, which still sinks too deep in the sand. Rocker-bogie would need 6 cm wheels to climb 5.5 cm, and that stands about 14 cm tall, which breaks under_sofa's 9 cm overhang. Tracks handle all three. Idler 6.5 climbs the 5.5 cm step, and the track top at 8.0 cm stays under 9 cm. A 24 cm contact length bridges about 10.8 cm, more than the 9 cm trench. About 190 cm2 of contact gives roughly 0.3 kPa, which sinks about 0.4 cm, far under the 3 cm belly (the tub top at 3+4 = 7 cm also clears the sofa). The tracks add mass and rolling resistance, and the 1.8 cm sprocket cuts top speed to about 0.45 m/s at 4.8 V. So the battery goes to a 2-cell Li-ion pack (18 rounds up to 2 cells, 18.8 Wh, 7.4 V, within the N20's 3-9 V). That gives about 1.5x the voltage, so about 0.69 m/s no-load, and about 1.5x the force of the two 100:1 N20s (about 16 N stall at the ground). It also doubles the usable energy at less mass than eight AA cells. Cost: $14 track kit plus $10.50 Li-ion ($24.50), 4 days, 57 machine min.

No parameter of bump_switch changes how far it senses, so the part has to change. The HC-SR04 ranges to 2 m in any light, ten body lengths ahead. That removes the 40 s of touch-and-back-off and lifts the 0.25 m/s cap: 12 m at about 0.5 m/s is roughly 25 s, under 45 s. The camera only lights 0.12 m in the dark, and the lidar cannot be supplied. Cost: $2.50 to buy an hc_sr04, 2 days.

Overall width is the 18 cm tub plus 3 cm of track on each side, which gives 24 cm. A tub width of 11 cm gives 17 cm overall. Adding the 1.20 cm steering error at full duty gives 18.2 cm, which leaves 1.6 cm of margin in the 19.8 cm opening, even at full speed. No tub width in range is too wide to fix with a parameter, so a swap isn't needed. The same width change passed bedroom in iteration 1 on the wheeled body. It costs $0 and about 100 machine minutes to reprint the tub, out of the 395 available.
